intro_html: Kerala beef fry, or ularthiyathu, is what happens when you refuse to stop cooking. The beef gets pressure cooked with spices until it is fall-apart tender, and then, instead of serving it, you dump it into a pan of caramelized shallots and curry leaves and dry-roast it until every drop of sauce is gone and the meat is dark, crusted, and coated in spice. That second stage is the entire dish. It is nothing like the two keema recipes in the library. This is dry, intense, and almost pure protein and spice.
cost_closing_html: About $3.07 a bowl for a South Indian beef fry with more spice concentration per bite than anything else we make.
shop_smart: Chuck roast is the right cut and the whole cost of the dish. It needs the pressure cooking to break down, so buy the cheap tough cut on purpose and shop the markdowns.
Ground fennel is the signature and it is a small jar. It is the warm licorice note that says Kerala, and one jar covers many batches.
Onions are the second component, not a garnish. A serious amount of sliced onion cooked down dark is what the beef gets coated in, and onions are cheap by the bag.
A pressure cooker or an instant pot pays for itself on dishes like this. Without one, this becomes a two-hour braise, which works, it just costs you the afternoon.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cut the beef chuck roast into bite sized cubes.
Toss the beef with the chili powder, ground coriander, ground turmeric, black pepper, garam masala, ground fennel, salt, most of the garlic, most of the ginger, and the diced yellow onion.
Pressure cook the seasoned beef with a small splash of water until it is completely tender, then open it up and boil off any remaining liquid.
Heat the vegetable oil in a wide heavy pan and cook the sliced red onions and sliced jalapenos slowly until deeply browned and sweet.
Add the rest of the garlic and ginger and cook until fragrant.

Add the cooked beef and dry-roast it over medium heat, stirring and scraping, until the moisture is gone and the meat is dark and crusted at the edges. This takes patience and it is where the dish is made.
Taste for salt, then cook the rice according to the package to serve underneath.
portion_html: Weigh the rice pot and the beef pan separately, subtracting the empty-pot weight from Step 1, and divide each by 14. Even rice base, even weight of beef. Every bowl comes in at 582 calories with 35 grams of protein. Because the sauce is cooked off, this reheats better than almost any curry and will not go soggy on you.
upsell_html: Intensely spiced dinners for about $3.07 a bowl. This is one of many. Members get every recipe in the Meal Prep section, plus the full library of money lessons, calculators, and tools, all for $1 a month.

head.description: Kerala beef ularthiyathu rebuilt for 14-serving meal prep: pressure-cooked chuck dry-roasted with browned onions and South Indian spices over rice. 582 calories, 35g protein, about $3.07 per serving.
head.keywords: beef ularthiyathu, kerala beef fry, south indian beef, pressure cooker beef, indian meal prep, dry roasted beef curry
steps: Cube the chuck roast and toss it with the ground spices, garlic, ginger, and yellow onion.
Pressure cook until completely tender, then boil off any leftover liquid.
Brown the sliced red onions and jalapenos slowly in oil until dark and sweet.
Add the remaining garlic and ginger and cook until fragrant.
Add the beef and dry-roast until the moisture is gone and the meat is crusted.
Cook the rice and portion the beef over it into 14 containers.
